title: Affine space
statement:
For a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], with the conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $n\in\mathbb N$, the affine $n$-space over $S$ is the scheme
$$\mathbf A^n_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb Z[x_1,\ldots,x_n])$$
with its first projection to $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Equivalently, this is the relative spectrum $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal O_S[x_1,\ldots,x_n])$, where the polynomial algebra sheaf is locally the polynomial algebra on $n$ variables. Over an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $S$, its restriction is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}(R[x_1,\ldots,x_n])$ with structure map induced by the inclusion of constants. For $n=0$, the projection $\mathbf A^0_S\to S$ is a canonical isomorphism; the notation $\mathbf A^0_S=S$ uses this identification. Smoothness is a separate statement, [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth].

blueprint_update.statement:
For a scheme $S$ and an integer $n\geq0$, the *affine $n$-space*
over $S$ is

$$
\mathbf A^n_S=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathcal O_S[x_1,\dots,x_n]\bigr)
$$

with its structure morphism $\mathbf A^n_S\to S$; for $n=0$ one has
$\mathbf A^0_S=S$.
